newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 20.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Thursday.
- Britain's biggest food store chain, Tesco, is poised to buy Ireland's biggest food retailer, the Quinnsworth group.
- The Irish government on Wednesday sanctioned a recruitment programme expected to create 1,000 new jobs in the Irish police force over the next three years.

- Irish political circles are awash with rumours that prime minister John Bruton will call an election within days. - Irish bond prices continued to slide on Wednesday, with fears of higher inflation and interest rates taking over from doubts about the plans for a single European currency as the focus of attention.
- Irish beef exports face a serious new challenge to their share of the Russian beef market following the lifting by Russia of a ban on beef from Argentina.

- Ireland's Police Commissioner and the main organisation representing rank and file Irish police have disagreed over the significance of a court ruling that police must identify informers to senior officers.
- Continuing speculation about a delay to the start of EU monetary union has led to a sharp fall in bond prices on the Dublin market and an increase in long-term interest rates.
- Road spikes can be used against car thieves by trained Irish police under strict supervision within days, Ireland's Justice Minister Nora Owen told the Irish parliament on Wednesday.
- It hardly seems 20 years since the phrase "May the force be with you" came into common usage but with a revamped 'Star Wars' is set to hit Irish cinema screens this weekend.
